sentence: This project studies how the rostromedial tegmental nucleus in the brains of mice contributes to the effects of opioids.
This project uses genomic methods to improve detection of treatment failure and to study what predicts malaria transmission.
This project builds mouse and cell models that help explain the mechanisms behind cancer development and how cancer responds to therapy.
This project studies how mitochondrial dysfunction in the intestinal epithelium contributes to inflammatory bowel disease.
This project studies how chemokine receptor signaling is controlled at the molecular level.
This project studies how germline stem cells in adults keep their identity while still changing state.
This project studies how the autophagy machinery affects dopamine 2 receptor metabolism and cocaine abuse.
This project builds non-invasive ways to diagnose invasive fungal disease in immunocompromised children using blood samples and AI analysis of CT scans.
This project builds statistical learning methods that use 3D brain images to help find biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.
This project studies how invasive breast cancer cells reprogram natural killer cells to promote metastasis.
This project studies how cell signaling drives the epithelial to mesenchymal transition and metastasis in breast, lung and other cancers.
This project builds a way to take high-resolution diffusion magnetic resonance imaging of microstructure with fast acquisition times.
This project gets information about vascular risk out of computed tomography scans of the carotid arteries.
This project studies how the brain produces speech and builds an intracortical brain-computer interface to restore communication in people with paralysis.
This project uses microglia and cerebral organoids to study how HIV and methamphetamine cause inflammation and damage in the brain.
This project studies how asymmetric cell division makes sister cells with different fates.
This project builds a center that aims to speed the translation of basic biomedical discovery into clinical application and better public health.
This project develops software for processing and analyzing nuclear magnetic resonance data on proteins and nucleic acids.
This project studies how exposure to pollutants called per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances and changes in serum glycosylation relate to inflammatory bowel disease risk.
